data.title: The Brass Bolt
data.text: You reached the sea without breaking the survey hut at Vell Foot. The hut still stands, with its kettle on the shelf. A new note on the door says someone went up to look for the stakes, could not find them, and left the tea. I do not recognize the handwriting, and nobody signed the note. The bolted stone still stands too. Tomas Lind set its brass bolt in 1979 and measured the glacier’s edge from it. By 1987, the edge was 212 metres from the bolt. He wrote that he measured the distance twice because he did not like the number. I know the feeling. I keep a sharp pencil.
